name: IoT Device Security Assessment
description: Security assessment of Internet of Things devices and their supporting ecosystems. Covers firmware analysis, credential auditing, network service evaluation, update mechanism integrity, physical interface exposure, cloud backend and API security, and mobile companion app assessment. Aligned with OWASP IoT Top 10 and ETSI EN 303 645.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to IoT security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the IoT attack surface and common vulnerability categories
evidence: Can describe the OWASP IoT Top 10 vulnerability categories
Aware of the end-to-end IoT attack surface: device, network, cloud, mobile app
Familiar with ETSI EN 303 645 consumer IoT security baseline

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Can perform structured IoT device assessment tasks under supervision
evidence: Tests IoT devices for default credentials and insecure network services
Extracts and examines firmware images for hardcoded secrets and known vulnerabilities
Evaluates basic cloud API and mobile app security with guidance
Documents findings against OWASP IoT Top 10 with supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses IoT devices and ecosystems end-to-end
evidence: Performs comprehensive device assessment covering firmware, services, update mechanisms, and physical interfaces
Evaluates cloud backend authentication, authorization, and data handling
Tests device-to-cloud communication for integrity and confidentiality
Produces IoT assessment reports with findings mapped to OWASP IoT Top 10 or ETSI EN 303 645

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex IoT ecosystems; develops assessment methodology; mentors others
evidence: Evaluates multi-device IoT deployments including provisioning, fleet management, and OTA infrastructure
Evaluates IoT communication protocol configurations and security (MQTT, CoAP, AMQP, Zigbee, BLE) in the context of device ecosystem assessment
Reviews and improves IoT assessments across the team
Develops IoT security assessment tooling and procedures

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's IoT assessment practice; publishes research; shapes standards
evidence: Established the lab's IoT security assessment methodology
Published research on IoT vulnerabilities, attack techniques, or security evaluation
Trains teams on IoT security assessment
Contributes to external IoT security standards or certification schemes

assessment_methods.description: Assess an IoT device end-to-end: firmware extraction, credential audit, network service enumeration, cloud API testing, and update mechanism evaluation
Review IoT assessment reports for coverage of OWASP IoT Top 10 categories and actionable mitigations

mitre_attack.note: ATT&CK does not comprehensively cover IoT; MITRE EMB3D is the primary threat model for embedded/IoT devices
